source_note: Agency-editable directory of custodian legal-process channels, compiled 2026-08-31 from each custodian's own published law-enforcement guidance (confidence noted per entry). VERIFY THE CHANNEL AT THE CUSTODIAN'S PUBLISHED GUIDELINES URL ON THE DAY OF SERVICE - portals, addresses and requirements change without notice, several custodians reject process sent to the wrong channel, and fake 'law-enforcement contact' emails circulate (see Bybit entry). Fallback when an entity is missing here: the SEARCH.org ISP List at https://www.search.org/resources/isp-list/. For offshore custodians, portals handle VOLUNTARY cooperation and preservation; compelled production formally requires MLAT through the DOJ Office of International Affairs.

custodians.process_notes: Verified 2026-08 (HIGH). All legal process via the Kodex portal (agency-email registration). Preservation requests accepted via portal without formal process. Subpoena -> subscriber/transaction records; court order -> non-content; warrant -> content. Freeze/seizure of funds requires a court order or seizure warrant. Foreign agencies: MLAT.

TOKEN ISSUER, not an exchange: Tether can freeze/blacklist USDT at ANY address - including self-custodied wallets - at the token-contract level, and has done so repeatedly on law-enforcement request. Email cited in Tether's published law-enforcement guidance (MED-HIGH confidence - verify at the guidelines URL). Request should identify the address, the USDT amounts and transactions, and the investigating agency; a court order strengthens but is not always required for an initial freeze.
